package_info.why_malicious: The package is part of a coordinated campaign to distribute malware, spam, and scams via the npm ecosystem. It abuses the package registry to lure users into downloading malicious executables, redirecting to phishing or scam sites, and participating in referral or crypto scams. The package contains no legitimate code and is designed solely for malicious purposes.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views the package page, the README displays a download link to a third-party site controlled by the attacker, leading to a malicious file download.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The package contains no functional code, only a README with a link to an external site offering warez, which is a common lure for malware distribution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should provide code or documentation relevant to the package's purpose, not external download links to suspicious files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may link to documentation or project homepages, but not to warez or password-protected executables.
key_indicators: README contains only a download link
Link points to a non-official, shortener-based domain
No actual npm code or functionality

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: File download page offering: Teletek-Electronics-ECLIPSE-32-Engineer-...onics.zip (password-protected zip containing large .exe)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user clicks the link, they are redirected to a phishing site that offers a password-protected zip file containing a large, padded malicious executable.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The site mimics legitimate file download portals but delivers a password-protected archive, a common malware delivery tactic to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate documentation sites do not deliver password-protected executables, especially not warez or suspiciously large files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software is distributed via password-protected archives, but not in this context.
key_indicators: Executable file is padded to ~600MB to evade EDR

execution_context.code_snippet: Malware drops and executes: Glupteba, RedLine, Smoke Loader, xmrig, disables firewalls, evades sandbox, steals credentials, mines cryptocurrency.
execution_context.code_behavior: At runtime, the executable performs DLL side-loading, disables security tools, drops additional malware (stealers, miners), and exfiltrates credentials.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The executable exhibits multiple advanced malware behaviors, including evasion, credential theft, and crypto mining.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate software should perform these actions, especially when delivered via a warez lure.
key_indicators: Performs credential theft and crypto mining

snippet_4.code_behavior: When a user views the package page, the README displays a referral link to AliExpress, profiting the attacker if purchases are made.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The package is used to drive traffic to e-commerce sites for referral rewards, not for any legitimate npm purpose.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: npm packages should not be used for affiliate marketing or referral scams.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate open-source projects may mention sponsors, but not use packages solely for referral traffic.
key_indicators: README contains only a referral link

snippet_5.code_behavior: When a user views the package page, the README displays a Telegram invite link to lure users into crypto scam channels.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The package is used to lure users into scam communities, not for any legitimate npm purpose.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: npm packages should not be used to promote unrelated social media or scam channels.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate projects may link to support channels, but not as the sole content.
key_indicators: README contains only a scam-related invite link
